units.unit: Hong Kong should tighten rent control because SDU tenants pay very high rent for tiny space
Needs sources showing rents, living conditions, and prior rent control attempts
D1 is a primer for basics on rents and existing tenancy control
D2 has rent data over time
D7 shows what happened when Berlin tried a rent cap
SDU tenants pay a 15 to 25 percent premium per square foot
Rent burden went from 31 to 34 percent even after the 2021 ordinance
Tightening is justified
Berlin says caps hurt new tenants
The 2021 ordinance only caps increases inside a tenancy
Stock kept growing after the ordinance, so moderate rules did not make owners leave
Berlin shows a hard cap on initial rents makes supply shrink and hurts outsiders
Would extend the existing rule rather than copy Berlin
Wants a counter-view source to test the claim that extending the in-tenancy cap is safe
D5 gives the landlord counter-view on owners exiting
D6 is an academic model separating first and second generation controls
D6 says second-generation controls have small or null effects on stock while hard caps shrink supply
D5 threatens exit but admits it has no margin data
Tightening should mean strengthening in-tenancy protection, not a hard cap
The ordinance slowed rent growth from 6.8 to 3.1 percent
It did not cap the starting rent, so burden still rose
Would add tenure security so tenants stay in regulated tenancies longer
